strategies.summary: Convert the input and folded weights to channels-last (NHWC) memory layout before the folded conv2d call in eval mode. cuDNN selects Winograd or TensorCore implicit-GEMM algorithms for 3x3 NHWC convolutions that are unavailable in NCHW, reducing effective DRAM traffic and improving L1/L2 reuse. Materialize the output contiguous before returning to preserve downstream shape contracts.

Precompute folded_weight in channels-last format and store as a module buffer to avoid per-call reformatting; invalidate buffer when switching between train and eval.
After the folded conv, call .contiguous() on the output only if the next op requires NCHW; profile to decide whether to leave it in NHWC.
Set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True in __init__ so cuDNN auto-tunes algorithm selection on the first eval call.
No changes to cuda_cu or cuda_cpp are required for this strategy.
strategies.expected_gain: 10â25% latency reduction from better cuDNN algorithm (Winograd 4x4/3x3 for 3x3 kernels), which lowers DRAM traffic versus standard implicit GEMM.
risk_notes: Output tensor will be in channels-last layout; ensure the benchmark harness or downstream ops accept NHWC or call .contiguous() before measurement.
Winograd introduces small numerical differences (~1e-5); verify correctness tolerance is compatible.
benchmark=True adds one-time algorithm search latency on the first eval forward pass.

Do not omit .contiguous() if downstream code assumes stride-1 innermost dimension.

review_notes.gemini-compatible: Using channels_last (NHWC) memory format is a proven way to accelerate cuDNN convolutions on modern GPUs by enabling faster Tensor Core algorithms.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import hashlib
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load_inline

_STARK_EXTENSION = None

def _stark_strip_anchor_markers(source: str) -> str:
    cleaned_lines = []
    for line in source.splitlines():
        stripped = line.lstrip()
        if stripped.startswith('# <<<IMPROVE:') or stripped.startswith('# <<<END_IMPROVE>>>'):
            continue
        cleaned_lines.append(line)
    return '\n'.join(cleaned_lines)

def _stark_extension_name() -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha1((_stark_strip_anchor_markers(CUDA_CPP_SRC) + _stark_strip_anchor_markers(CUDA_CU_SRC)).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:12]
    return f'stark_cuda_l2_p73_{digest}'

def _stark_get_extension():
    global _STARK_EXTENSION
    if _STARK_EXTENSION is None:
        _STARK_EXTENSION = load_inline(
            name=_stark_extension_name(),
            cpp_sources=_stark_strip_anchor_markers(CUDA_CPP_SRC),
            cuda_sources=_stark_strip_anchor_markers(CUDA_CU_SRC),
            functions=None,
            extra_cflags=['-O3'],
            extra_cuda_cflags=['-O3', '--use_fast_math'],
            with_cuda=True,
            verbose=False,
        )
    return _STARK_EXTENSION

# <<<IMPROVE:user_helpers>>>
# <<<END_IMPROVE>>>

CUDA_CPP_SRC = r"""
# <<<IMPROVE:cuda_cpp>>>
#include <torch/extension.h>

// Add pybind exports for custom CUDA entrypoints here.
PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME, m) {}
# <<<END_IMPROVE>>>
"""

CUDA_CU_SRC = r"""
# <<<IMPROVE:cuda_cu>>>
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <cuda.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

// Add CUDA kernels and exported wrapper functions here.
